label: MySQL
migrationTool: versioned SQL files applied by the project's migration runner
notes: Every change is a new timestamped SQL file; an applied migration is never edited.
DDL is not transactional in MySQL: keep one DDL statement per file where possible and verify each file on a disposable copy before a shared environment.
Authorization is enforced with database grants; there is no row-level security, so tenant filtering lives in the application data layer and is tested.
Destructive changes need owner approval and a `mysqldump` first.
Credentials come from the environment and are never committed.
